historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Average of the base-case 10-year revenue path (8.0% fading to 3.5%), anchored to raised FY2026 guidance of ~8% total/organic growth. Equity CAGR rejected as a growth proxy (see warning).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3.6% 5y, 0.1% 3y) diverges >30% from revenue (4.6%/4.1%) and EPS (8.2%/6.6%) because TRI returns >100% of FCF (dividends, $1.0B/yr buybacks, the $605M May-26 return of capital) -- book value is not a growth measure here.
historical_growth.notes: All windows start FY2020/FY2022 -- never across the FY2017 Refinitiv (F&R) structural break, and FY2019 (OCF $702M trough) is excluded from endpoints. Reported revenue CAGRs understate organic growth (~7% organic in 2025) because of non-core disposals (FindLaw etc., Dec-2024) and Global Print decline. GAAP EPS is distorted by LSEG disposal gains (FY2021, FY2023) and a $468M FY2024 tax benefit. Owner-FCF CAGR (OCF - capex - SBC) is in line with reported FCF CAGR -- SBC (~1.5% of revenue) is not growing faster than cash flow.

scenario_narratives.base: Big 3 (82% of revenue) keep compounding at ~9-10% organic near term as CoCounsel lifts price/mix on Westlaw, Practical Law and Checkpoint; Global Print declines and Reuters is flat-ish, so total organic growth fades from ~8% to 3.5% by year 10 as AI tools become table stakes rather than an upsell. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands ~270bp on operating leverage, then holds as AI compute is reinvested.
scenario_narratives.bull: CoCounsel converts its 1M+ user lead into a paid agentic tier priced on work product rather than seats; the Third Circuit Ross Intelligence ruling forces AI rivals to license TRI content. Big 3 organic growth stays at 10%+ for several years, total growth holds 9%+ and adjusted EBITDA margin reaches ~45% on the fixed editorial/content base.
scenario_narratives.bear: Agentic AI compresses billable research hours and the per-seat model: Harvey, LexisNexis Protege and foundation-model vendors bid down legal/tax research pricing, large firms build in-house tools, and renewals reprice lower over the 1-5 year contract cycle. Growth fades to ~2.5%, adjusted EBITDA margin gives back ~3pp to ~37%, capex stays at 8.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Thomson Reuters is valued as a mature, subscription-heavy information and workflow-software franchise on an owner-FCF basis: SBC (~1.5% of revenue) expensed, leases charged in the flows, organic growth only (acquisition spend not modelled), USD WACC 8.0%. The share price has fallen from ~$164 to ~$99 on AI-disintermediation fears; the valuation question is how much of the content moat survives agentic AI, which is carried in the 25% bear weight and a bear path with falling margins rather than in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI disintermediation of per-seat legal/tax research pricing (Harvey, LexisNexis Protege, foundation models, in-house tools)
Terminal value is ~70%+ of EV; a 20x cap on terminal FCF is assumed in the base
Acquisition spend ($0.8-1.0B/yr) excluded: if growth depends on it, the organic paths are too high
Woodbridge ~71% control limits any takeover premium
US concentration (72% of revenue) and government-contract exposure
Derived (not printed) period-end share count, ~0.2% uncertainty

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 76.28-164.30
data_sources.financials: TRI_Metrics.csv (FY2015-FY2025, interims to Q2-2026); FY2025 annual report (adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, FCF reconciliation, 2026 outlook, lease note); Q2-2026 report (balance sheet at 30-Jun-2026, EPS share-count note, return of capital note 14, lease principal)
data_sources.qualitative: TRI_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): segment mix, raised FY2026 guidance after Q2-26, CoCounsel adoption, Ross Intelligence appellate ruling

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, estimated at 30-Jun-2026: Q2-26 weighted basic 438.4M (H1-26 report note on EPS) less the May-4-2026 share consolidation (~6.5M shares, 0.984560 ratio) for the two post-consolidation months and the 1.1M Q2 buybacks, plus 0.12M vested DSUs and 0.11M option/TRSU dilution = ~436.2M. The H1 report does not print a period-end count; this is derived and could be off by ~1M (0.2%). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks (FY2025 $1.0B, H1-26 $362M) fund the flat count and more.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, employee-benefits note 'Share-based payments' ($111M); equity-award withholding taxes not separately disclosed (parser found none) and treated as immaterial. TRI's adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back SBC, so the EBITDA margin path below is adjusted EBITDA + SBC (pre-SBC) and the engine deducts SBC once.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo chart API, NYSE/Nasdaq USD line)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.8 for a subscription-heavy (81% recurring) legal/tax information franchise -> cost of equity ~8.2%; debt is ~5% of capital at ~4.5% after tax, so WACC ~8.0%. One WACC across all scenarios: the AI-disintermediation risk is priced in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash outflow (principal $64M + interest, total lease cash outflows $83M in FY2025 incl. short-term) charged at 1.0% of revenue inside EBIT; lease liabilities ($241M at 30-Jun-2026: $60M current + $181M non-current, inside 'Other financial liabilities') EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is set slightly below reported depreciation + software amortization to approximate ex-right-of-use depreciation, so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are attributable.
inputs.timing_note: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30-Jun-2026 (FY2025 $7,476M + H1-26 $4,041M - H1-25 $3,685M = $7,832M), so year 1 is the twelve months to Jun-2027 and the flows line up with the 30-Jun-2026 net debt and share count. Using FY2025 revenue with June net debt would have counted H1-26 free cash flow twice (once in the flows, once in the share count it bought back).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: profitable, mature content/workflow software operating company, IFRS, Canadian filer reporting and quoted in USD -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations for leases). No prior DCF or memory entry; fresh build. Net debt = commercial paper $1,618M + long-term notes $1,323M - cash $577M at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-26 report balance sheet), excluding leases (treatment B). Net debt rose from $1,612M at Dec-25 because the May-26 $605M return of capital/share consolidation plus $362M of H1 buybacks exceeded H1 FCF. Not in the bridge, deliberately: (1) ~$430M of UK Diverted Profits Tax paid 2015-18 and carried as receivables from HMRC/indemnity counterparty (management expects a substantial refund; litigated, timing unknown) -- upside of up to ~$1/share; (2) the defined-benefit pension deficit (material plans 94% funded) -- downside of similar order. They roughly offset and both are excluded. The $238M liability for the pre-defined broker repurchase plan is an equity commitment, not debt, and is excluded. Acquisition spend ($0.8-1.0B/yr historically) is NOT modelled; growth paths are therefore organic-only (FY2026 guidance ~8% total = organic). Interest income is not stripped because the company is net debt. last_fcf = TRI-defined FY2025 FCF $1,952M (OCF 2,651 - capex 634 + other investing 1 - lease principal 64 - preference dividends 2) less SBC $111M; it is after ~$143M of net interest, so it understates the unlevered flow the engine projects.

bear.narrative: Agentic AI compresses billable research hours and the per-seat model: Harvey, LexisNexis Protege and foundation-model vendors bid down legal/tax research pricing, large law and accounting firms build in-house tools on licensed or public data, and renewals reprice lower over the 1-5 year contract cycle. Growth fades to ~2.5% (Print and Reuters drag, Big 3 mid-single digit), adjusted EBITDA margin gives back ~3pp to ~37% under price pressure and AI compute cost, and capex stays elevated at 8.5%.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC margin = TRI adjusted EBITDA margin + SBC (FY2025: 39.3% + 1.5% = 40.8%). FY2026 guide +100bp adjusted (~40.2%) -> ~41.7% pre-SBC for calendar 2026; the Jul-26/Jun-27 year 1 at 42.0%, then operating leverage on a fixed cost base partly reinvested in AI compute, maturing at 43.5% (adjusted ~42%).
base.da_pct_note: FY2025 depreciation $111M + software amortization $721M = $832M (11.1%); FY2026 guide $890-910M. Set slightly below to strip ROU depreciation, and converged toward capex+0.3pp by year 10 because the acquired-software amortization that keeps D&A above capex is fed by acquisitions this model does not charge.
base.capex_pct_note: Accrued capex 8.2% of revenue FY2025, ~8.0% FY2026 guide; cash capex $634M (8.5%) in 2025. Held at 8.2%.
base.cash_tax_note: Adjusted ETR 18.5% (2025), ~19% guided 2026; cash taxes ex-disposal items ~17-19% of pretax. Ramped to 21% for Pillar Two and US mix.
base.wc_note: Prepaid subscriptions: deferred revenue $1,251M at FY2025 (+$189M). ~15% of the revenue increase captured as cash.
base.narrative: Big 3 (82% of revenue) keep compounding at ~9-10% organic near term as CoCounsel lifts price/mix on Westlaw, Practical Law and Checkpoint; Global Print declines and Reuters is flat-ish, so total organic growth fades from ~8% to 3.5% by year 10 as AI tools become table stakes rather than an upsell. Margin expands ~270bp on operating leverage, then holds as AI compute is reinvested.

bull.narrative: CoCounsel converts its 1M+ user lead into a paid agentic tier priced on work product rather than seats; the Ross Intelligence appellate win forces AI rivals to license TRI content, turning content into a royalty stream. Big 3 organic growth stays at 10%+ for several years (inside management's 8-11% TAM growth), total growth holds 9%+ and adjusted EBITDA margin reaches ~45% as the fixed editorial/content base is leveraged.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the one axis that matters -- whether agentic AI disintermediates per-seat legal/tax research -- is genuinely unresolved and the market has de-rated the stock ~40% from its 52-week high on exactly that fear. Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice in 2026 and Big 3 organic growth is accelerating (10% in Q2-26), so the evidence to date sits with the base path. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs both sustained 10%+ Big 3 growth and a new AI pricing model to stick, two independent things going right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
